clue.text: Surgery ensured their numbers were up

definitions.text: Surgery ensured their numbers were up

parts.words: Surgery ensured their numbers were up
parts.note: read as singers whose operation kept their voices high, so the 'numbers' (songs) they sang were pitched up, not that a count rose

explanation.surface: A hospital report boasting that operations increased the patient count.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Numbers were up' suggests statistics rising; here numbers are songs, sung in a high register by boy singers castrated before puberty in past centuries.
explanation.definitionFit: Castrati were male singers gelded as boys so their voices stayed soprano or alto, letting them sing high.

clue.text: Dispatched to give a worker a break — are you fonder of him?

indicators.note: giving a break means splitting the worker phrase open so another word goes in

parts.note: a worker is a worker bee
sent means dispatched

explanation.surface: Sent off so that an employee can rest, and missed all the more for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the saying 'absence makes the heart grow fonder'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone away from home is the one an absence makes the heart grow fonder of.

clue.text: Dog keeps new queen calm

indicators.note: keeps means the word for dog holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: to dog someone is to trail them

explanation.surface: A hound looks after a fresh monarch serenely.
explanation.definitionFit: Tranquil and calm are synonyms for peaceful and undisturbed.

clue.text: Legendary ship back over river

indicators.note: over places the word for back around the river letter

parts.note: ago means back in time, as in years back

explanation.surface: A mythical vessel sails back across a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a reversal sign but is AGO, which goes 'over' R.
explanation.definitionFit: Jason and the Argonauts sailed in this ship of Greek myth in search of the Golden Fleece.

clue.text: Strip of land is therefore to have motorway through

indicators.note: through means the motorway runs inside the word for therefore

parts.note: thus means therefore
M is a British motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A narrow piece of land must accordingly have a major road built across it.
explanation.definitionFit: An isthmus is a narrow neck of land connecting two larger landmasses.

clue.text: Some time before spring, frozen

indicators.note: before puts the time word in front of the word for spring

parts.note: a spell is a period of time
a bound is a leap or spring

explanation.surface: A cold snap arrives before the season of spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' suggests the season but is a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone spellbound is rooted to the spot, transfixed, as if frozen.

clue.text: Cross stream initially in dark

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Cross stream initially in dark (3-5)': JET (stream) and BLACK (dark) fit, but 'Cross' and 'initially' give no letters in any parse; likely an OCR misreading not confirmed by any source.

clue.text: Spies those closest as source of warmth

parts.note: moles are spies planted inside an organisation
kin are one's closest relatives

explanation.surface: Agents keep their nearest and dearest around for comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: Moleskin is a thick cotton fabric used for warm trousers and clothing.

clue.text: See group changing mind, acting as conscience

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of the two words are being rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A gathering of people altering its views and serving as a moral guide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges the letters of SEE and GROUP.
explanation.definitionFit: In Freudian theory the part of the psyche that acts as a moral conscience is called by this name.

clue.text: One continually moving house set about packing goods

indicators.note: packing means the outer letters hold another piece inside them, as a case holds its contents
about signals that the little word set is turned around into a different order

parts.note: cargo is goods carried by a ship or plane

explanation.surface: Someone forever relocating, with a set of belongings around the packed goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' suggests a home move; the creature carries its shell. 'about' rearranges the three-letter word as EST, which wraps the goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A snail carries its shell wherever it goes, so it is always moving house; escargot is French for snail.

clue.text: Roll back into bottomless pit, close to demise — though can be pulled out?

indicators.note: into means the reversed roll goes inside the word for the pit

parts.note: hell is traditionally described as the bottomless pit

indicators.note: back says the word for roll is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: a bap is a soft bread roll in Britain

indicators.note: close to means only the final letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A grim scene of falling into an endless abyss near death, yet with hope of rescue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns BAP into PAB, set 'into' HELL; 'close to' demise gives E. A BAP is a British bread roll.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who can be pulled out of trouble is capable of being assisted, which is the sense of this adjective.

clue.text: Slow after second vehicle was stopped in its tracks

indicators.note: after places the word for slow behind the other pieces

parts.note: a truck is a goods vehicle
dumb can mean slow-witted

explanation.surface: A slow vehicle comes to a sudden halt after a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Being made speechless with shock is like being halted abruptly, as an animal frozen in place.

clue.text: Boy wants to serenade new neighbour of Chelsea

parts.note: Ken is a boy's name
to serenade someone is to sing to them

explanation.surface: A lad longs to sing under the window of someone new next door.
explanation.walkthrough: KENSINGTON and Chelsea are adjoining districts of west London, forming one borough.
explanation.definitionFit: This west London district borders the district named, sharing a borough with it.

clue.text: Second, or reverse

definitions.meaning: to second a proposal is to support it
to reverse a car is to move it rearward

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to support someone and to drive in the rearward direction.

clue.text: Start to fail in business after a month

indicators.note: after places the month in front of the word for business, with 'in' a link

parts.note: Dec is the abbreviation for December
a line of business is one's trade

explanation.surface: A company begins to falter a month after starting trading.
explanation.definitionFit: To go into a gradual weakening is to begin failing, a near synonym.

clue.text: Council vehicle cuts out during run

indicators.note: during puts the jumbled letters inside the word for run

parts.note: to dart is to run quickly

indicators.note: out signals the letters of cuts are put out of order

explanation.surface: Local services get reduced while the bus is running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges CUTS as USTC, placed 'during' DART. A dustcart is a British rubbish lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: The rubbish lorry is run by the local council in Britain to collect household waste.

clue.text: Commentary upon being put in prison

indicators.note: being put in means the word for upon goes inside the word for prison

parts.note: a cage is a prison
over means upon, as in a coat over a shirt

explanation.surface: A broadcaster's remarks about someone being jailed.
explanation.definitionFit: Media coverage of an event is the reporting and commentary given on it.

clue.text: Ballet shoe, type that's short? No, it's big, yellow, and round

parts.note: a pump is a light flat shoe like a ballet slipper

indicators.note: short tells us the last letter of the word for type is cut off

parts.note: kind means type or sort

explanation.surface: A list of things that are small, contrasted with something large, golden and spherical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's short' trims KIND to KIN; the 'No' denies the smallness the earlier words suggest.
explanation.definitionFit: A large orange-yellow gourd is the classic big round fruit, here described rather than named by synonym.

clue.text: Faint having injected speed, heading to therapist for source of information

indicators.note: having injected means the speed unit goes inside the word for faint

parts.note: pale means faint, as in a pale colour
mph, miles per hour, is a measure of speed

indicators.note: heading means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone feeling weak after a drug injection goes to a counsellor for advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injected speed' suggests drugs; speed is MPH, and 'heading to' gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: A pamphlet is a small leaflet that supplies information.

clue.text: Popular Greek character near death needing oxygen, it's suggested

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
end means death
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A well-liked Greek man close to dying needs an oxygen supply.
explanation.definitionFit: An innuendo is a remark that hints at something without saying it, implied rather than stated.

clue.text: Entering Cambrian epoch up in outer space

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the hidden letters are read from bottom to top
entering means the letters sit inside the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A geologist enters the Cambrian period in a study of the cosmos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entering' takes the run RIANEPO from Cambrian epoch, and 'up' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The open air is the outdoors, the space outside buildings, punningly called outer space.

clue.text: Saint offered prayer to deliver from evil

parts.note: an Ave is the Hail Mary prayer

explanation.surface: A holy man prays to be rescued from wickedness, as in the Lord's Prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescue or redeem someone from sin is the religious sense of this verb.

clue.text: Let people, in time, dip crackers

indicators.note: in puts the word for people inside the jumbled letters
crackers means crazy, so the letters of time and dip are jumbled

parts.note: men means people

explanation.surface: Allow folk to dunk biscuits in due course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' looks like biscuits but is the anagram signal, giving IMPEDIT. 'Let' is a noun here, as in tennis or the phrase without let or hindrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A let is an obstruction, as in the legal phrase without let or hindrance.

clue.text: Warmer town in Wales

definitions.meaning: a warmer here is a garment that keeps you warm, a knitted jacket
a coastal town in west Wales

explanation.definitionFit: The knitted button-up jacket is named after an earl whose title came from the Welsh town of the same name.

clue.text: Male charging fifty on board

definitions.meaning: a charging male animal, like a rampaging steer
on a dartboard the inner centre scores fifty

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a male bovine that charges and the dartboard centre worth fifty points.

clue.text: A question? One's the limit — how nosy some appear!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
the line marks the limit, as in drawing the line

explanation.surface: Asking a single question is the most you can do, being so inquisitive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nosy' means having a nose, not prying: a hooked nose is described this way.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a hooked, eagle-like nose, so some people appear this way in profile.

clue.text: Pasta — I fix a load for a start

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Pasta — I fix a load for a start (8)': RIG A TON + I gives the answer, but I stands first in the clue and 'for a start' has no job; the OCR text may be garbled and no source confirms it.
annotationWithheld.clue: Pasta — I fix a load for a start

clue.text: The story of my wife?

definitions.meaning: an account or narrative of events
a wife is a family member, related by marriage

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a narrated account and a person connected by family or marriage.
